product.name: Boundary First UX
product.primaryLine: Design the boundary, not the screen.
product.productPromise: Make complex systems tangible, navigable, testable, and repairable without losing the larger context.
product.northStar: Oh. I can see the system now.

hero.eyebrow: BOUNDARY FIRST UX · WORKING PUBLIC STANDARD
hero.title: Design the boundary, not the screen.
hero.deck: Every interface is a bounded representation of a larger system. Boundary First UX makes those boundaries explicit so users can change resolution, perspective, and context without losing identity, provenance, consequence, or closure.

opening.title: Every interface is a boundary.
opening.body: The design problem is not only what appears on the screen. It is what the representation admits, excludes, compresses, reveals, makes actionable, and preserves as context changes.

flagship.title: The Green Project Was Inside a Larger System
flagship.premise: A locally valid project view hides a ten-year maintenance obligation outside the project boundary. The user discovers the obligation, reframes toward consequence, traces it through handoff and funding, promotes the representation into lifecycle context, repairs ownership, and reaches scoped closure.
flagship.desiredReaction: Oh. I can see the system now.

timelineProof.question: What ends here?
timelineProof.reveal: Project closeout occurs while a ten-year maintenance obligation begins and household service consequence persists.
timelineProof.promotion: Expand the two-year project view into a twelve-year lifecycle while preserving the original project interval.
timelineProof.line: The project ends. The system does not.

rendererIndependence.thesis: Boundary First semantics belong to the represented world, not to any one renderer.

semanticRule: Views do not own semantic truth. Renderers receive semantic state and emit declared intentions.

grammar.closureRule: Closure is a state, not a verb or button.

conceptualTangibility.artDirection: scientific instrument + civic infrastructure + museum cutaway + drafting table + playful game logic
conceptualTangibility.rule: Every physical metaphor must have operational semantics.

requirements: no color- or position-only essential information
accessibility.rule: An accessible representation is a lawful projection, not a fallback copy.

questions: Is the represented containment boundary explicit?
Is partiality visible rather than hidden?
Are identity and provenance preserved through transformations?
Can state be recovered after a transformation?
Can hidden structure be revealed without destroying context?
Is the experience semantically complete through accessible routes?

notThis: claim that existing design systems are obsolete

sandbox.title: NOW BREAK IT
sandbox.promotionRule: Sandbox contact may produce evidence, defects, or reusable methods. It never promotes an object directly to capability, program, or canon without the corresponding review gate.

closing.title: Design the boundary, not the screen.
closing.body: Make complex systems tangible without erasing the larger system that gives the local view meaning.
